stories.headline: Powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake strikes Colombia, killing at least 111 people
stories.body:
A powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake has struck Colombia, killing at least 111 people, injuring 87 others, and causing 61 buildings to collapse across the country [c1]. The earthquake was measured at magnitude 7.4 by both the US Geological Survey and Colombia's national authority [c5]. Its epicenter was located near the Tatama National Nature Reserve on the eastern border of Choco province, approximately 30 kilometers from Cartago [c7]. Less than an hour after the primary earthquake, the US Geological Survey recorded a 5.0-magnitude aftershock [c8].

The severe shaking caused extensive damage to public infrastructure and residential areas throughout the country [c6]. Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella reported that 1,575 homes were damaged, 37 homes were completely destroyed, 18 health centers were damaged, and 52 schools were damaged across Colombia [c6].

The metropolitan area of Pereira was particularly hard hit by the disaster [c3]. Officials reported that 40 people died in the Pereira metropolitan area, 65 buildings collapsed, and people were trapped inside 15 of those collapsed structures [c3]. In response to the crisis, the mayor of Pereira, Mauricio Salazar, declared a state of public calamity, manifest urgency, and a nighttime curfew in several districts [c2].

Damage was also reported in other towns and cities across the region [c10]. In Manizales, one of the towers of the city's neo-Gothic cathedral collapsed during the earthquake and fell directly onto the nave [c10]. Due to the widespread danger and destruction, civil aviation authorities suspended flight operations at multiple airports, including those in Pereira, Manizales, Quibdo, Armenia, Cartago, Buenaventura, and Cali [c9].

International assistance has begun to arrive as rescue operations continue [c4]. Ecuador's President Daniel Noboa Azin offered Colombia 47 specialized rescuers, search dogs, and equipment to assist in response efforts [c4]. Colombia has suffered deadly seismic events in its past, including a 6.2-magnitude earthquake near Armenia in 1999 that killed more than 1,100 people [c11].

vocab.meaning: the point on the Earth's surface directly above where an earthquake starts
a smaller earthquake that follows a larger earthquake
an event causing great and sudden damage or distress

stories.headline: Netanyahu rejects US Gaza peace plan and demands full Hamas disarmament
stories.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has publicly rejected a US-backed peace proposal for Gaza, insisting that no military withdrawal can happen until Hamas is fully disarmed [c13]. The 15-point peace plan, proposed by Donald Trump, called for Hamas to surrender its weapons, the creation of an international stabilization mechanism, and a progressive withdrawal of Israeli forces [c12].

Netanyahu's public rejection blindsided Israeli military commanders, who had discussed withdrawal plans in Rafah with him just days earlier [c14]. The rejection came as US Central Command chief Adm Brad Cooper visited Israel to urge officials to work toward ending military operations in Gaza, Lebanon, and Iran [c15]. Currently, Israeli forces control more than 60 percent of the territory in Gaza [c19], and more than 73,300 people have been killed in Israel's offensive since October 2023 [c20].

Despite his firm rhetoric, Netanyahu scaled back airstrikes in Gaza by requiring targeted killings to be authorized directly by the IDF chief of staff rather than regional commanders [c16]. According to a senior US official quoted by journalist Barak Ravid, the White House understood Netanyahu's political needs ahead of Israel's upcoming election and was unbothered by his statements as long as attacks remained restrained [c17]. Meanwhile, construction of the first base for an International Stabilization Force is scheduled to begin in Rafah at the end of August 2026 [c18].

vocab.meaning: the reduction or withdrawal of military weapons
caught completely unprepared by surprise
kept under control or limited in extent

stories.headline: Ukrainian drone strike on Russian oil refinery kills 13 people
stories.body:
A Ukrainian drone strike on the city of Nizhnekamsk in Tatarstan, Russia, located about 750 miles from the border, has killed at least 13 people [c21]. Local officials reported that 75 people were injured and one child was killed in the attack [c26]. The strike targeted the Taneco oil refinery, which is owned by the company Tatneft [c22]. Tatarstan regional head Rustam Minnikhanov stated that nine people died when a drone hit a hostel building [c23]. The Uzbek consulate in Tatarstan confirmed that seven of the victims killed in the attack were citizens of Uzbekistan [c24].

Russia's Defence Ministry claimed its air defenses intercepted 456 Ukrainian drones overnight across Russian territory and Crimea [c27].

In other international developments, the World Health Organization reported that a warehouse in Ukraine's Dnipro region was struck twice in 24 hours, destroying $500,000 worth of medical supplies [c28]. In Sweden, security service Säpo shut down a Russian intelligence operation involving three people working under diplomatic cover [c25]. Germany announced it will double personnel in its federal police anti-drone unit to 300 after finding an explosive drone at Leipzig-Halle airport [c29]. In Estonia, the governing coalition lost its parliamentary majority when two MPs left their parties, leaving the government with 50 of 101 seats [c30].

vocab.meaning: an industrial plant where raw materials like oil are processed
an establishment providing inexpensive food and lodging
stopped or caught something before it reached its destination

stories.headline: Heatwaves and drought trigger widespread water restrictions in Western Europe
stories.body:
Severe heatwaves and intense drought have forced nations across Western Europe to implement strict water restrictions [c33]. Nearly 70 percent of France, covering 67 out of 101 departments, has been placed under the highest crisis alert level for water-use restrictions [c33]. Weather agency Météo-France warned that temperatures would reach nearly 40°C in southeastern France, following a national record high of 44.3°C set on June 23 [c34]. July wildfires in southwestern France forced the evacuation of 220,000 people from their homes [c36].

The extreme weather extends across the region [c35]. England and Wales recorded their driest July since 1836, with 19 counties in England receiving no rain for the entire month [c35]. Western Europe experienced its hottest June and July on record, with average temperatures reaching 21.62°C, which is 2.79°C above normal [c38]. European climate agency Copernicus reported that July for Europe as a whole was the 11th warmest on record [c39]. Copernicus also noted that global extrapolar sea surface temperatures reached a record average of 20.96°C in July [c37].

In the United States, July was the hottest month ever recorded in 132 years of record-keeping, with temperatures 3.3°F above average [c31]. Wyoming recorded its hottest July on record, at 5.1°F above normal [c32].

vocab.meaning: sharing a common border or touching along a boundary
the movement of people away from a dangerous place
situated or occurring outside of the polar regions

stories.headline: Russian court bars anti-war Yabloko party from State Duma elections
stories.body:
Russia's Supreme Court has upheld a lawsuit by the Rodina party to bar the liberal, anti-war Yabloko party from competing in upcoming State Duma parliamentary elections [c40]. The Rodina party's lawsuit accused Yabloko of supporting an extremist organization and committing copyright infringement by quoting a Soviet-era song [c43]. Outside the courthouse, Yabloko leader Nikolai Rybakov stated that the party intends to appeal the decision [c41]. An earlier 2026 poll showed Yabloko had 3 percent public support, below the 5 percent threshold needed to win seats in the State Duma [c42].

The ruling comes amid a broader crackdown on Yabloko members and political opposition in Russia [c44]. In June, senior Yabloko member Maxim Kruglov was sentenced to seven years in prison over social media posts about civilian casualties in Ukrainian cities [c44]. In 2025, Kremlin critic and Yabloko politician Lev Shlosberg was charged with spreading false information about the Russian military [c46]. Meanwhile, public support for Russia's ruling United Russia party has fallen to 33 percent [c45].

vocab.meaning: an action that breaks a law, rule, or agreement
a level or point at which something starts or applies
severe enforcement of discipline or restriction

stories.headline: WHO reveals DR Congo Ebola outbreak began months before official declaration
stories.body:
The World Health Organization (WHO) revealed that the current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo began in February, three months earlier than its official declaration on May 15 [c47]. WHO Africa director Dr. Mohamed Janabi announced that genetic sequencing confirmed the earlier timeline [c47]. The DR Congo health ministry has reported 4,294 confirmed cases and 1,960 deaths caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola [c48].

Dr. Janabi stated that health workers are reaching only about 30 percent of Ebola cases due to widespread insecurity in eastern DR Congo, leaving the remaining patients to die at home [c49]. The current outbreak is the fastest-growing on record, reaching 1,000 deaths faster than the 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak [c50].

To help combat the disease, the WHO has recommended initiating full-scale human trials for the Ervebo vaccine to assess whether it provides cross-protection against the Bundibugyo strain [c51].

vocab.meaning: determining the order of genetic material in an organism
a state of danger or lack of safety in an area
protection against one strain achieved through vaccination against another

stories.headline: Typhoon Dolphin forces over 1 million evacuations in eastern China
stories.body:
Tropical storm Dolphin brought heavy rainfall and severe flooding across eastern China after making landfall as a typhoon on Sunday [c52]. Dolphin hit land in Taizhou, Zhejiang province, with maximum sustained winds of 151 kilometers per hour [c53]. Chinese authorities were forced to relocate more than 900,000 people in Wenzhou, 150,000 in Fujian, and 200,000 in Shanghai [c54]. A central Shanghai weather station recorded 313 millimeters of rainfall in 24 hours, the highest 24-hour total in over 150 years of record-keeping [c57]. On Monday, Shanghai's two main airports cancelled 943 flights after cancelling over 1,300 flights before landfall [c55].

The storm's broader system affected surrounding regions [c56]. Typhoon Dolphin drove temperatures in Hong Kong to a record high of 36.9°C on Sunday [c58]. In Okinawa, Japan, the storm injured six people and cut power to over 50,000 buildings [c59]. In the Philippines, monsoon rains enhanced by Dolphin triggered a landslide in Baguio, bringing the death toll in northern Luzon to 15 [c56].

vocab.meaning: the arrival of a storm or typhoon over land
to move people to a new place to live or stay
increased or made stronger in effect

stories.headline: Trump signs executive order seeking changes to childhood vaccine schedule
stories.body:
US President Donald Trump has signed an executive order directing major changes to the CDC childhood immunization schedule and calling for the combined MMR vaccine to be split into three separate shots [c60]. Trump claimed in the Oval Office that children should receive vaccines across multiple doctor visits instead of getting several shots on a single day [c64]. He also claimed that receiving MMR vaccines together could be lethal and attributed high autism rates to vaccine volume [c62]. Republican Senator Bill Cassidy criticized the order on social media, writing that it is wrong and stating that vaccines do not cause autism [c63].

The executive order retains full routine recommendations for only six of 17 childhood vaccines, protecting against 11 diseases [c61]. Trump announced that his administration will no longer recommend hepatitis B, Covid-19, or influenza vaccines for children [c67]. Currently, separate individual vaccines for measles, mumps, and rubella are not licensed or available for children in the US [c65]. Trump previously issued a vaccine directive in December 2025, but subsequent policy changes were blocked by a federal court [c66].

vocab.meaning: the process of making a person immune to an infectious disease
officially authorized or given legal permission
an official instruction or order from an authority

stories.headline: Student protests over exam leaks spark violent clashes and political tension in Jharkhand
stories.body:
Widespread anger over recruitment exam irregularities has led to violent clashes between student protesters and police in Ranchi, Jharkhand, triggering political turmoil and demands for official investigations [c68, c70]. Thousands of job aspirants marched toward the Jharkhand state assembly to protest against reported exam leaks [c70]. To prevent demonstrators from storming barricades near the state legislature, police used water cannons, tear gas, and batons [c71]. Demonstrators emphasized the intense competition for employment in the state, pointing out that a recent recruitment drive had attracted nearly 640,000 applications for just 2,025 open posts [c72].

The exam scandal has already led to official action within the state's testing authority [c73]. The former chair of the Jharkhand Public Service Commission was arrested over exam irregularities, and three commission members subsequently resigned [c73]. However, student leaders rejected government claims that 98 percent of their demands had been met, stating that officials had cancelled only three of the 13 requested exams [c75].

The crisis quickly escalated into a national political confrontation [c68, c69]. Outside the chief minister's residence, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leaders Babulal Marandi and Aditya Sahu led a protest demanding a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) inquiry into the leaks before being detained by police [c68]. In Delhi, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi held a press conference condemning police violence against the peacefully protesting students [c69]. In response, Union Minister JP Nadda accused Rahul Gandhi of spreading misinformation regarding claims that pellet guns were used against student protesters at Jantar Mantar [c76].

Meanwhile, Jharkhand Chief Minister Hemant Soren released an open letter regarding the situation [c74]. Soren thanked security agencies for handling the student protests with restraint and urged students not to fall into political traps [c74].

vocab.meaning: people who are ambitious to achieve or gain something
temporary barriers put up to block movement
increased rapidly in intensity or seriousness

stories.headline: Indian Parliament passes Tribunals Reforms Bill to create new national commission
stories.body:
The Lok Sabha has passed the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, by voice vote without debate amid persistent protests from Opposition members [c77]. The legislation establishes a New Delhi-based National Tribunals Commission composed of a chairperson and four members, including two judicial members and two technical members [c78]. The bill repeals the previous Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021, which was struck down by the Supreme Court for violating judicial independence [c79].

Under the new law, tribunal chairpersons will serve five-year terms up to age 70, while members will serve five-year terms up to age 67 [c82]. Establishing and operating the new commission and its secretariat is estimated to cost ₹27.14 crore [c83]. The bill places 16 tribunals under commission oversight [c80]. While it excludes the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT), it includes the NCLT's appellate forum [c80].

The reform comes as Indian commercial tribunals struggle with severe operational delays [c81]. An analysis by think tank DAKSH showed that commercial tribunals in India face a backlog of more than 356,000 cases worth ₹24.72 trillion, managed by just 350 members [c81].

vocab.meaning: concerned with dealing with applications for decisions to be reversed
an accumulation of uncompleted work or matters
an administrative office or department
